assumptions: Load: GSE P50 hourly projection 2027-2030; 2031-2032 = 2030 profile x 3.69 %/yr (mean GSE growth 2026-2030).
Net interconnector flow fixed to the 2025 monthly balance (import as supply, export as load) in dispatch; adequacy uses domestic load only (exports are interruptible) and the fixed import.
Tbilsresi III + IV (272 MW) retired from 2027; Tkibuli (13 MW, no output in 2024-2025) excluded; other units stay.
Lead times: RICE available from 2028, CCGT-3 from 2029 at the earliest.
Battery 200 MW / 200 MWh from 2029 (enters at the end of 2028), 92 % per-way efficiency, 10 % minimum SoC.
Ruisi wind 206 MW from 2027 with the Kartli capacity factor (43 %).

Scenario A: no other new plants. Scenario B: linear build-out to the PLEXOS 2030 wind (1,909 MW) and solar (1,496 MW) fleet and its additional run-of-river energy (~2,013 GWh) by 2030, constant after 2030.
Hydrology: mean of 2024 and 2025 (base); 2025 = dry, 2024 = wet sensitivities.
Leap years 2028 and 2032 are modelled with 8,760 hours (29 February omitted, as in the GSE projections).
Thermal efficiency/VOM: PyPSA generic; gas 5.5 USD/MMBtu, coal 4.0 USD/MMBtu (illustrative, review required).
Candidates: CCGT-3 250 MW (PyPSA 2030 CCGT costs) and RICE in 20 MW blocks (assumed 850 USD/kW, 46 %); 8 % discount rate, 25-year life.
Forced outages: generic two-state Markov rates (CCGT 4 %, old steam 10 %, OCGT 5 %, coal 15 %, RICE 2 %); no planned maintenance; hydro units not outaged (energy is their binding limit).
Adequacy target LOLE <= 3 h/year; hydrology sampled 50/50 from 2024 and 2025.

Reserve requirement = largest unit + P99 of the unpredictable hourly wind/solar change (Gori profiles, single-site, conservative; PLEXOS ramps are implausible); headroom = unused thermal and regulating-hydro capacity in the dispatch (battery not counted).
Single node: no transmission limits, no N-1 network security, no AC power flow.
